title: Deciduous and Evergreen Trees
seo_title: Year 1 Science: Deciduous and Evergreen Trees Worksheets (Naming Trees)
standard_text: Identify and name a variety of common wild and garden plants, including deciduous and evergreen trees.
meta_desc: Free Year 1 science worksheets on trees: deciduous and evergreen trees, naming trees from acorns, conkers, cones and leaves, the parts of a tree and a tree survey. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Evergreen trees keep their leaves all year round.
body_html:
How to think about it

Deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn.

  • Evergreen trees keep their leaves all year.
  • Oak, beech and sycamore are deciduous.
  • Holly, pine and fir are evergreen.
Example

An oak in winter?

It loses its leaves in autumn

Answer: bare: deciduous

Example

A pine in winter?

It keeps its needles

Answer: green: evergreen

Common mistakes

  • Thinking evergreen trees never lose a single leaf.
  • Thinking a bare tree in winter is dead.
  • Thinking conkers come from oak trees.

faq.a: A tree that loses its leaves in autumn and grows new ones in spring, such as an oak, beech or sycamore.
A tree that keeps its leaves all year, such as a holly, pine or fir. It drops a few old leaves at a time, never all at once.

faq.q: How can we name a tree?
faq.a: Look at its leaves, bark, seeds and fruits. Acorns come from oaks, conkers from horse chestnuts and cones from pines.
